new_translation.translation_scope: Source statements are preserved as translated, including unverified historical, linguistic, scientific and character claims. Their translation is not independent verification.

existing_editorial.identity: Existing project editorial drafts with source bibliography. Secondary references were read through these local drafts only; their linked remote publications were not fetched or independently rechecked.
existing_editorial.locator_policy: Heading locators are supplied for local drafts. Precise printed page numbers for the external bibliography are not present in the local drafts and are not invented.

global_omissions: All attributed birth-character and horoscope readings are omitted from display copy.
No fixed good/bad fortune is assigned to a sign, and no specific trecena interpretation is generalized to every date with that sign.
Speculative etymologies, genetic memory, lunar control of human behavior, bioenergy, telepathy and other unverified scientific assertions are excluded.
Named religious figures in display are contextual associations, not universal patron assignments. Sign, numeral, year and trecena roles remain separate.
No source names, citation markers, edition claims or editorial cautions appear in display copy.

cipactli.name: Cipactli

newer_section_notes.supporting_note: The source introduces the first day sign, records several animal translations, and gives its own proposed analysis of the name.
The source associates Cipactli with early life, emergence from water, Tamoanchan, and the Earth. It links the flint fangs with its account of ancestral knowledge.
The Ita Andehui quotation connects the fantastic crocodilian being with beginnings and the name Cipactonal.
The source attributes energetic leadership, initiative, tenacity, firm principles, and responsibility to birth under this sign.
Captions identify plate 75 of the Nuttall Codex and the Stone of the Suns.
This entry has no explicit ruling-figure subsection; its discussion does not supply a separate patron assignment.

description.supporting_notes: First sign; crocodilian strength, marsh and land imagery, earth and origins. Creation-body account comes from the existing editorial context; field-ridge comparison comes from the newer translated testimony on page 115.

xochitl.name: Xochitl

newer_section_notes.supporting_note: The source identifies Flower as the final day sign and includes reported comparisons of flowers with beauty, fragrance, songs, work, and completed tasks.
The source presents flowering as an image for positive qualities, thoughts, expressions, activity, and the satisfactory completion of aims.
The source relates sensitivity and the sharing of feeling through poetry, song, music, dance, painting, and the phrase flower and song.
The source attributes creativity, subtlety, steady purpose, clear speech, and enduring will to people associated with Xochitl, using flowering and fruitfulness as its comparisons.
The caption identifies Xochitl in Bodley Codex plate 33.
